full_judgment:
2. The appellants as plaintiffs filed the said suit for permanent injunction restraining the defendants from evicting them from the suit land alleging that the suit land was purchased by Rebati Mohan Dey, father of the plaintiffs and after his death plaintiffs inherited the same and they have been in exclusive possession of the same. The defendant Nos. 1 and 8 in collusion with the employees of the Settlement Department got their names entered in the rent rolls along with the names of the plaintiffs father although they have no title and possession in the suit land. Defendant Nos. 1 and 8 in collusion with other defendants has been trying to dispossess the plaintiffs from the suit land and so the suit was filed. 

 6. It appears that the learned Munsif although decreed the suit on the basis of possession he also found, in substance, that the father of the plaintiffs Rebati Mohan Dey purchased the suit land by utilizing joint family fund and the father of the plaintiffs and the defendants paid rent for the suit land. He, however, found that in a suit for permanent injunction title need not be gone into and he discussed the evidence of both sides and came to the findings that the plaintiffs were in exclusive possession of the suit land. The learned appellate Court below also found possession of the plaintiffs but held that as they are co-sharers the plaintiffs cannot restrain them permanently by an order of injunction. It also drew adverse inference against the plaintiffs for not admitting the case of the defendant Nos. 1 and 8 that they are co-sharers in the suit land. 

 9. It is an established principle of law that possession of one co-sharer is for all and every co-sharer has a right to possess every piece of joint property and such possession of one co-sharer cannot be adverse to other co-sharers unless a clear case of ouster is proved. But if a co-sharer is found to be in exclusive possession the other co-sharers out of possession can dispossess him whether in due course of law and in such a case a decree for permanent injunction may be granted. The learned appellate Court below observed that 'the plaintiffs having tried to deny the title of the defendants they are not entitled to the equitable relief of injunction. But I am of the opinion that although it is found by both the courts concurrently that the plaintiffs and defendant Nos. 1 and 8 are co-sharers, the plaintiffs being in exclusive possession they are entitled to the relief by way of permanent injunction. The learned appellate Court below erred in law in dismissing the suit and should have affirmed the decree passed by the trial Court. But this decree of permanent injunction shall not be treated as ouster of defendant Nos. 1 and 8 from the suit-land for the purpose of a suit for partition for other purpose. With these observations the appeal is allowed and the judgment and decree passed by the learned appellate Court are set aside and those passed by the learned Munsif are restored.
